title: Final Parking Space: 1971 Cadillac Coupe de Ville

body_markdown:
After nearly three years of this series, we’ve admired four Cadillacs in their final parking spaces ([a ’48 Series 62 Touring Sedan](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/final-parking-space/final-parking-space-1948-cadillac-series-62-touring-sedan/) , a[’78 Eldorado Biarritz](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/final-parking-space/final-parking-space-1978-cadillac-eldorado-custom-biarritz-astroroof/) , an[’82 Cimarron](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/final-parking-space/final-parking-space-1982-cadillac-cimarron/) , and an[’87 Allanté](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/final-parking-space/final-parking-space-1987-cadillac-allante/) ), but what about the best-selling Cadillac model of most of the 1960s and 1970s? It’s time for a De Ville, clearly, so I found this ’71 at[a boneyard in Sparks, Nevada](https://www.picknpull.com/locations/70/sparks-nv) .


Cadillac


Cadillac introduced the De Ville name in 1949, when it was a trim-level designation for an upscale version of the Series Sixty-Two two-door.


Cadillac Division, General Motors


The first use of the Sedan de Ville name was on a special trim level for the 1956 Sixty-Two four-door hardtop.


Cadillac Division, General Motors


For the 1959 model year, the De Ville became a model name in its own right. The Coupe de Ville was built through 1993, while the Sedan de Ville lasted all the way through 2005.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Cadillac went back and forth with spelling and capitalization in its De Ville marketing materials and car emblems over the decades, but the most common usage was “de Ville” when following “Cadillac,” “Coupe,” or “Sedan,” and “De Ville” when on its own. Sometimes it was “DeVille” with no space. You’ll see “DeVille” and “de Ville” in the same Cadillac brochure on occasion, so it appears that GM’s style guide wasn’t consistent. The phrase essentially means the same thing that “Town Car” did at Lincoln, going back to the horse-drawn carriage era, but French and thus classier. The three versions in the illustration above are from, top to bottom: 1998, 1988, and 1962.


Cadillac Division, General Motors


GM did a full restyle of its big luxury cars for the 1971 model year, making the De Ville a bit bigger and roomier and a lot smoother-looking. The Cadillac Calais, essentially a less swanky De Ville, got the same treatment. This generation of De Ville was built through the 1976 model year, after which it got a significant downsizing.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


For 1971, the engine was a Quadrajet-topped 472-cubic-inch V-8 rated at 345 horsepower and 500 lb-feet of torque. This meant 30 fewer horses and 25 fewer pound-feet versus the 1970 version, thanks to a reduction in the compression ratio from 10:1 to 8.5:1, but it also meant that the car would be happier running on regular gasoline.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


This engine has an HEI distributor, which means a distributor (or maybe an entire engine) swap from a 1974 or later Cadillac has taken place. The 500-cubic-inch engine, which had been exclusive to the Eldorado since being introduced[for 1970](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/klockau-classics/1970-cadillac-fleetwood-eldorado-8-2-liter/) , was used in the De Ville for the 1975 and 1976 model years.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The interior is crispy after decades of sitting outdoors in the high desert sun.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The vinyl top appears to have been nuked completely off the car.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


If there’s any serious rust-through on this car (other than in the usual areas around the edges of the vinyl top), I didn’t see it.


Cadillac Division, General Motors


The MSRP for the 1971 Coupe de Ville was $6264, or about $51,715[in 2026 dollars](https://murileemartin.substack.com/p/your-handy-inflationary-car-price) . You could get[the Calais coupe](https://oldcarbrochures.org/United%20States/Cadillac/1971_Cadillac/1971%20Cadillac%20Prestige/slides/71cad24-25.html) for $5899 that year ($49,292 today), making the Coupe de Ville the second-most-affordable Cadillac for 1971.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Amazingly, air conditioning wasn’t standard equipment on the ’71 De Ville; you had to pay $537 for the thermostat-equipped Automatic Climate Control system to get it (that’s $4505 in today’s money). The[cheapest new 2026 car Americans can buy](https://murileemartin.substack.com/p/these-1988-new-cars-were-cheaper) has air conditioning at no extra cost.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


As far as I can tell, Cadillac never offered this kind of velour upholstery in the 1971–76 De Ville. These seats are either reupholstered or swapped in from a more affordable, same-generation GM C-Body (perhaps an Olds 98).


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The Buick “wire wheel” hubcaps (upgraded with Cadillac center emblems) in the trunk suggest a fair amount of parts mixing-and-matching over the decades.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Courtesy Honda in Reno[still sells used non-Honda cars](https://www.billpearcehonda.com/used-vehicles/?certified=false&min-year=1960&fq=1&max-year=2027) , but I think this license plate frame goes back to[the early days of the dealership](https://www.billpearcehonda.com/about-us/) .


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The 1971–76 generation of De Ville proved to be a real showroom success, with more than 600,000 units sold. However, production across all GM divisions was down for the 1971 model year, due to[a massive strike that began in late 1970](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/international-review-of-social-history/article/gallant-fight-the-uaw-and-the-1970-general-motors-strike/4D5EA265031DE961F29C167C21CBDC89) , and so only 135,426 De Villes were made for that year. The peak sales year for the 1971–76 De Ville was 1973, with 216,242 sold.


Cadillac Division, General Motors


The year of overall Peak de Ville turned out to be 1977, when 262,171 De Villes purred out of Cadillac showrooms.


You knew it, even back then, that someday— *someday* — you’d own a Cadillac.


If you ran your new ’71 Cadillac on leaded gas, you’d put five pounds of melted lead toy soldiers into the air, with another handful of soldiers melting in your muffler and on your spark plugs.
